title: Logistics Coordinator - Operations & Quality
company: Pearson Whiffin Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Logistics Coordinator - Quality and Operations

£30,000 - £31,000

Monday to Friday, office-based position

Mid Kent

We are currently supporting a well-established manufacturing business in the Maidstone area with the recruitment of a Logistics & Quality Coordinator.

This is a varied role suited to someone who enjoys a combination of coordination, administration and hands-on operational work. You'll work closely with teams across the business, including production, warehouse and logistics, helping to ensure orders are prepared and dispatched accurately and on time.

The role would suit someone with experience in dispatch, logistics, warehouse administration or manufacturing, who is comfortable working across both office and operational environments.

Duties:
- Coordinating deliveries and collections with transport providers
- Preparing shipping and delivery documentation and keeping records up to date
- Using an ERP system to process orders, stock movements and dispatch information
- Carrying out basic quality and quantity checks before goods are dispatched
- Monitoring stock levels and supporting inventory checks
- Liaising with customers and internal teams regarding deliveries and order requirements
- Supporting the warehouse and production teams with picking, packing and preparing goods for dispatch
- Investigating and escalating any delivery, quality or operational issues
- Producing basic reports and maintaining accurate administration
- Working in line with company health and safety procedures

What We're Looking For:

We're looking for someone who is naturally organised, practical and enjoys working in a busy environment. You don't need to have experience in every part of the role, but you'll ideally bring some experience from a logistics, dispatch, manufacturing or warehouse setting.

You'll be confident using computer systems, comfortable dealing with different people throughout the day and have a good eye for detail. Experience with SAP or another stock/ERP system would be useful.

The role also has a hands-on element, so you'll need to be happy getting involved on the operational side rather than being purely office-based. Experience with deliveries, transport companies, stock or quality checks would be a bonus.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone reliable, proactive and willing to get stuck in.

This role is being handled by Holly Ensoll and Chloe Wadhams Recruitment Consultant for Pearson Whiffin Recruitment.

title: Part Time Administrator
company: Hill McGlynn Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Accounts & Office Administrator - Part-Time
Location: Maidstone, Kent
Salary: £14.50 - £15.50 per hour
Hours: 20 hours per week across 4 days
Start: Immediate
Working Pattern: Office-based Friday working required

The Opportunity
Hill McGlynn is recruiting on behalf of an established contractor based in Maidstone for a part-time Accounts & Office Administrator to join their team.
Working within a close-knit office, this is a varied position combining accounts, office administration, health & safety and general business support. In many respects, the role will act as the central point of support for the office, making it well suited to someone who enjoys taking ownership and being involved across different areas of a business.

The environment is fast-paced and busy, so our client is looking for someone organised, proactive and comfortable managing several priorities at once.

The Role
Responsibilities will include:
- Managing accounts payable processes, including checking, processing and chasing invoices
- Collecting, checking and consolidating employee timesheets
- Supporting the day-to-day administration and organisation of the office
- Maintaining accurate financial and administrative records
- Using Xero to support accounts and finance processes
- Assisting with internal and external audits and ensuring relevant documentation is maintained
- Supporting health & safety administration and procedures
- Maintaining and updating company documentation and records
- Providing general administrative support to the wider team
- Assisting with additional office, accounts and compliance duties as required

About You
We are looking for someone who:
- Has previous experience within accounts, finance administration, office administration or a similar role
- Has experience using Xero
- Is confident managing accounts payable and invoice processes
- Is highly organised with excellent attention to detail
- Is comfortable working within a fast-paced and varied environment
- Can confidently manage multiple responsibilities and deadlines
- Has a proactive approach and is happy to take ownership of tasks
- Is a strong communicator and comfortable working within a small, close-knit team
- Is able to work throughout the school holidays
- Is available to work Fridays

Previous experience within the construction industry or a construction-related consultancy would be advantageous but is not essential.

Hours & Location
This is a 20-hour-per-week position across four days, with flexibility around the daily start time. Friday must form part of the working week.

The position is fully office-based in Maidstone, with no hybrid working available.

Due to the office location, being able to drive would be advantageous, and on-site parking is available.

What's on Offer?
- £14.50 - £15.50 per hour, depending on experience
- 20 hours per week across four days
- Flexibility around start times
- Immediate start available
- On-site parking
- Varied role with involvement across accounts, administration, health & safety and general office management
- Opportunity to become an integral part of a busy team

If you are an organised and reliable administrator looking for a varied part-time opportunity in Maidstone, we would be keen to hear from you.
Apply now with your CV or contact Hill McGlynn for further information.

title: Clinical Administrator
description: This is a key role within our multidisciplinary team, supporting clinicians by ensuring incoming clinical correspondence is reviewed, processed and accurately recorded. You will identify relevant clinical information, update patient records and ensure correspondence is directed to the right person or team. The role will suit someone who enjoys working with detailed information, follows processes carefully and can use their judgement to identify what can be safely managed and what needs clinical input. You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. As a Clinical Administrator, you will help keep the practices clinical and administrative processes running smoothly. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence. You will also monitor recalls, screening results and high-risk medication monitoring to help ensure important follow-up is not missed. The role includes supporting QOF, audits, enhanced services and other quality improvement work, alongside patient recall programmes such as immunisations and cervical screening. You will also process insurance and medical reports, monitor the practice email account and provide wider administrative support when required. Working closely with the clinical team, you will identify and escalate complex or sensitive issues appropriately and support effective communication across the practice. You will also contribute to team meetings and training and help new colleagues learn practice processes. High standards of confidentiality, information governance and accuracy are essential. Job Description Clinical Administrator Job Title: Clinical Administrator Responsible to: Administration Lead, Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Partnership Hours: TBA Job Summary The Clinical Administrator provides vital support to the multidisciplinary team by managing and processing clinical correspondence and patient records in line with practice and national guidelines. The role focuses on streamlining workflows to reduce unnecessary GP administration, ensuring accurate coding and filing of information, and directing more complex items to the appropriate clinician for review. The post-holder will work as part of the Clinical Administration team, prioritising their workload effectively, maintaining strict confidentiality at all times, and knowing when to escalate matters to supervisors or clinicians. Roles and Responsibilities Ensure all incoming and internal correspondence is stored in patient records. Review and Read Code clinical correspondence before forwarding to clinicians. Process and file hospital letters, reports, emails and other correspondence. Code diagnoses, procedures and investigations accurately. Refer complex or high-risk documents, including safeguarding issues, to the relevant clinician. Summarise new patient records (manual and GP2GP) and process registrations, transfers, and out-of-area notifications. Manage incoming test results, redirect unmatched pathology, and process screening and monitoring results (e.g. diabetic eye screening, mammograms, DMARD recalls). Process Out of Hours reports and other external communications. Maintain accurate documentation for insurance reports, medical reports and private letters. Monitor the practice email inbox, flagging urgent queries promptly. Support enhanced service administration, QOF monitoring, recalls (e.g. immunisations, smears, chronic disease), and audits. Run EMIS searches as required. Provide administrative cover for other team members when necessary. Open, scan, distribute and file post; manage photocopying and record requests. Assist with training and mentoring of new staff. Maintain a tidy office environment and adhere to a clear desk policy. Teamwork & Communication Work as part of the Clinical Administration Team and the wider practice team. Build effective working relationships with colleagues, patients and external organisations. Communicate clearly and professionally, ensuring confidentiality at all times. Participate in meetings and training, including occasional sessions outside normal hours. General Responsibilities Confidentiality Patients entrust the practice with sensitive information and staff must respect this confidentiality at all times. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues or the practice may only be shared in line with GDPR and practice policies. Health & Safety Follow practice health and safety policies, including infection prevention and control. Use personal security systems as required. Identify risks, manage work safely, and report concerns promptly. Maintain work areas in a safe, hazard-free condition. Equality & Diversity Promote equality of opportunity and respect the rights of patients, carers and colleagues. Act in ways that recognise diversity and ensure fairness, consistent with policy and legislation. Respect privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs at all times. Personal & Professional Development Participate in annual appraisal and performance reviews. Take responsibility for ongoing learning and development. Share skills and knowledge with colleagues and support new staff training. Quality Strive to maintain quality and safety within the practice. Contribute to audits, QOF and CQC compliance. Reflect on individual and team activities, suggesting improvements to enhance performance. Manage own time, workload and resources effectively. Communication Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external agencies. Adapt communication methods to meet individual needs and ensure understanding. Other Information Duties may change according to practice needs, following consultation and training. The role is subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act (1974) exceptions, requiring disclosure of relevant convictions. The practice operates a non-smoking policy.
